Surah 109: al-Kafirun is Meccan, and it has six verses.

In the Name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshipers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped, nor are you worshipers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾

(p-521) This surah is Meccan according to the majority of scholars. It is narrated from Qatadah that it is Medinan. The reports mention as its occasion of revelation that they said to him, peace and blessings be upon him: "Leave what you are upon, and we will make you wealthy, marry you to whichever of our noble women you wish, and make you a ruler over us. And if you will not do this, then worship our gods, and we will worship your God, so that we share [in this matter]. Thus, whatever good there is, we will all attain it." Since most of those who hated him were from Quraysh, and they asked him to worship their gods for a year and they would worship his God for a year, God Most High revealed this surah as a disavowal of them and an announcement, beyond any doubt, that this would not happen. In His saying "Say" there is evidence that he was commanded to do so by God. His addressing them with "O disbelievers" was in their assemblies and in places where they stretched out their hands, and the disparagement in the description is evidence that he was protected by God Most High and did not care about them. The disbelievers are specific people, and they are those who said that statement to him: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, Umayyah and Ubayy, the two sons of Khalaf, Abu Jahl, the two sons of al-Hajjaj, and their counterparts from among those who did not become Muslim and died in disbelief, confirming the announcement in His saying: ﴿nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾. Regarding these sentences, the exegetes have several opinions:

The first: they are for emphasis. So His saying ﴿nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped﴾ is an emphasis of His saying ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾, and His saying ﴿nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾ the second time is an emphasis of His saying ﴿nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾ the first time. Emphasis is very common in the language of the Arabs, and they have related from it verse and prose in quantities that can hardly be counted. The benefit of this emphasis is to cut off the hopes of the disbelievers and to confirm the announcement that they will die in disbelief and will never believe.

The second: it is not for emphasis. They differed. al-Akhfash said: the meaning is "I do not worship now what you worship, nor are you worshipers of the year what I worship, nor am I a worshiper in the future of what you have worshiped, nor are you worshipers in the future of what I worship." Thus emphasis disappears, since each sentence is restricted to a different time.

Abu Muslim said: the "ma" in the first two is in the sense of "alladhi" (which), and the intended meaning is the worshiped object; the "ma" in the latter two is verbal (masdariyyah), meaning: I do not worship your worship, which is based on doubt and abandoning reflection, nor do you worship the like of my worship, which is based on certainty. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: since His saying "I do not worship" could mean "now", leaving the future open to what will happen, the clarification came with His saying ﴿nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped﴾ forever and as long as I live. Then came His saying ﴿nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾, the second, as a decisive statement that they will never believe in Him, like one who unveils the unseen. This is like what was said to Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]. As for whether this applies to specific individuals, while the people of Noah were generalized in that, this is the meaning of the repetition in the surah, and it is of supreme eloquence, and it is not mere repetition; rather, what I have mentioned is in it. End of quote.

al-Zamakhshari said: "I do not worship" is intended to refer to worship in the future, because "la" (not) only enters upon an imperfect verb with the meaning of the future, just as "ma" only enters upon an imperfect verb with the meaning of the present. The meaning is: I will not do in the future what you ask of me of worshiping your gods, nor will you do in it what I ask of you of worshiping my God.

﴿nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped﴾, that is: and I was never a worshiper in the past of what you worshiped in it; meaning: no worship of an idol was known from me in the time of ignorance, so how could it be expected from me in Islam? ﴿nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾, that is: and you did not worship at any time what I am upon in worship. If you say: why was it not said "what I have worshiped" as it was said "what you have worshiped"? I say: because they used to worship idols before the sending of the Prophet, and he had not been worshiping God Most High at that time. End of quote.

As for his restriction in His saying "because 'la' does not enter" and in His saying regarding "ma" that it does not enter, this is not correct; rather, that is the usual case with both, not an absolute rule. The grammarians have mentioned the entry of "la" upon the imperfect meaning the present, and the entry of "ma" upon the imperfect meaning the future, and that is recorded in the extended works of grammar. For this reason Sibawayh did not present it with a restrictive particle; he only said: "la" is negation of the saying "he does", and the act has not occurred; and he said: as for "ma", it is negation of the saying "he is doing", when it is in the state of doing. So he mentioned the usual case for both.

As for his statement in His saying ﴿nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped﴾, that is: and I was never a worshiper in the past of what you worshiped in it, this does not stand, because "'abid" is an active participle that has governed ﴿what you have worshiped﴾, so it is not interpreted as past; it is interpreted as present or future. His view on the active participle is not the view of al-Kisa'i and Hisham, who permit it to govern in the past tense.

As for his statement in His saying ﴿nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾, that is: and you did not worship at any time what I am upon in worship, then "'abidun" has governed "what I worship", so it is not interpreted as past. As for his saying "and he had not been" to the end, it is a breach of courtesy toward the station of prophethood. It is also incorrect, because he, peace and blessings be upon him, was never other than one who affirmed the oneness of God, Mighty and Majestic, exalting Him above everything unbefitting His majesty, shunning their idols, and making the pilgrimage to the House of God, standing at the sacred places of Abraham, peace be upon him; and these are acts of worship to God Most High. And what worship is greater than affirming the oneness of God Most High and rejecting their idols? Knowledge of God Most High is among the greatest acts of worship. God Most High said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56]. The exegetes said: its meaning is "that they should know Me"; so God Most High named knowledge of Him worship.

What I choose in these sentences is that first He negated His worship in the future, because "la" usually negates the future. It is said: then He joined to it ﴿nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾, a negation of the future by way of contrast. Then He said ﴿nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped﴾, a negation of the present, because the active participle's real indication is the present. Then He joined to it ﴿nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾, a negation of the present by way of contrast. Thus the meaning is consolidated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, does not worship what they worship, neither now nor in the future, and they likewise, since God has decreed that they will die in disbelief. And since He said ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾, using "ma" for the idols, the speech was matched by the "ma" in "what I worship", even though it is intended to be God Most High, because in contrast there is allowed what is not allowed when standing alone. This is according to the view of those who say that "ma" is not used for individuals who know; as for those who permit it, and it is attributed to Sibawayh, there is no need for an excuse by contrast. It was also said: "ma" in "what I worship" is masdariyyah, and it was said: it is so in all of them. al-Zamakhshari said: what is intended is the attribute, as if it were said: I do not worship falsehood, and you do not worship the Truth.

﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾, that is: for you is your polytheism and for me is my monotheism. This is the utmost in disavowal. Since the more important thing was his, peace and blessings be upon him, being free of their religion, He began with negation in the preceding sentences with the attribute to him. And once the negation was established, He returned to address them in His saying ﴿For you is your religion﴾, as a form of conciliation, and it is abrogated by the verse of the sword. Salam read "dini" with a yā’ both in pausal and continuous recitation, and the seven readers omitted it. And God knows best.
